building.name: 2022 Connecticut State Building Code (2021 International Building Code portion, with Connecticut amendments)
building.edition: 2022 Connecticut State Building Code with Errata #1, on the 2021 International Building Code
building.quote: 2022 Connecticut State Building Code (w/ Errata #1) ED: October 1, 2022 [...] (Amd) 101.1 Title. The 2021 International Building Code as amended in this section shall be known as the 2021 International Building Code portion of the 2022 Connecticut State Building Code. (Add) 101.1.1 Statutes. Pursuant to sections 29-252a and 29-253 of the Connecticut General Statutes, respectively, this code shall be the building code for all towns, cities and boroughs and all state agencies. [Office of the State Building Inspector page] The 2022 Connecticut State Building Code (CSBC) is based on the International Code Council's widely-adopted 2021 International Codes and references the ICC A117.1-2017 standard for accessibility. It applies to projects with permit applications filed from October 1, 2022.
building.no_local_amendments_quote: [Conn. Gen. Stat. Sec. 29-253(a), as quoted in the state pack] The State Building Code, including any amendment to said code adopted by the State Building Inspector and Codes and Standards Committee, shall be the building code for all towns, cities and boroughs.

scheduled_change.what: The 2026 Connecticut State Building Code (expected to adopt the 2024 International Building Code, 2024 International Existing Building Code and 2024 International Plumbing Code, with Connecticut amendments) was expected to take effect on July 1, 2026. It is still awaiting approval by the Legislative Regulation Review Committee of the General Assembly and the effective date has been delayed; no new date is given. When it takes effect it will apply to projects whose permit is applied for after the effective date, with a code modification ("grace period") available for about three months.
scheduled_change.quote: The next state building, fire safety, and fire prevention codes were expected to take effect on July 1, 2026, but at this time, we await approval of the next codes by the Legislative Regulation Review Committee of the Connecticut General Assembly, and therefore the effective date has been delayed. [...] The following model codes are anticipated to be adopted by the 2026 Connecticut state codes: 2024 International Building Code (IBC) by ICC; 2024 International Existing Building Code (IEBC) by ICC [...] 2024 International Plumbing Code (IPC) by ICC [...] The new codes will apply to projects for which a permit is applied for after the effective date.

permit.exempt_list_quote: [2022 Connecticut State Building Code, (Amd) 105.1 Required] Any owner or owner's authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building or structure [...] shall first make application to the building official and obtain the required permit. [(Amd) 105.2 Work exempt from permit] Exemption from the permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws, statutes, regulations or ordinances of the jurisdiction. Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area is not greater than 200 square feet (18.58 m²). 2. Fences, other than swimming pool barriers, not over 7 feet (2134 mm) high. 3. Oil derricks. 4. Retaining walls that are not higher than 3 feet (914 mm) [...] 5. Water tanks supported directly upon grade [...] 6. Sidewalks, driveways and on-grade concrete or masonry patios [...] 7. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work not involving new construction, structural changes or alterations. 8. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 9. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Use Group R-3 occupancy [...] 10. Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes and not including service systems. 11. Swings and other playground equipment. 12. Window awnings in Group R-3 and U occupancies [...] 13. Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not higher than 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) and not containing any electrical, plumbing or mechanical equipment. 14. Portable grandstands or bleachers providing seating for fewer than 100 persons when located outside of a building. [(Add) 105.2.2 Repairs] Application or notice to the building official is not required for ordinary repairs to structures, replacement of lamps or the connection of approved portable electrical equipment to approved permanently installed receptacles. Such repairs shall not include the cutting away of any wall, partition of portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load-bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress [...] [City of Hartford, Division of Licenses and Inspections, handout "Work Exempt From Permits"] 105.2 Scope and Administration, Work Exempt from Permits [...] Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: [...] 7. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. [...] 13. Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) height.
permit.partitions_named_note: Toilet partitions are not named in the state list or in the city's handout. The only partitions listed are 'nonfixed and movable' ones not higher than 5 feet 9 inches; toilet partitions are anchored to the floor, wall or ceiling. Item 7 covers 'similar finish work' only where it involves no new construction, structural changes or alterations. Whether a like-for-like replacement is an 'ordinary repair' under Section 105.2.2 is not stated. The city's handout (a PDF created February 2022) reproduces an older model-code list (120 square foot sheds, 4 foot retaining walls) and leaves out the state's words 'not involving new construction, structural changes or alterations' in item 7 and 'not containing any electrical, plumbing or mechanical equipment' in item 13; the state code's text governs.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Hartford job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Connecticut building rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Hartford insurance offices, state buildings, hospitals and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Connecticut's building rules, which Hartford enforces unchanged, set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Hartford follows Connecticut's statewide permit rules. They require a permit to alter or repair a building and list the work that needs none. The list covers painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work that involves no new construction or alterations, and movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask Hartford's Licenses and Inspections division (860-757-9200) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.install_rule: Hartford's municipal code sets no city contractor license or registration, and building permits come from the city's Licenses and Inspections division. Connecticut doesn't require a state contractor license to install toilet partitions in typical commercial buildings. A Major Contractor registration applies only to large structural work on very large buildings. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: When a contractor applies for a Hartford building permit, the city asks for the contractor's current license and a workers' compensation insurance certificate that names the City of Hartford.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, city, town and school projects costing $100,000 or more for remodeling or repair, or $1 million or more for new construction, Connecticut law requires at least the wage the state Labor Commissioner sets for each trade in each town. For a carpenter on building work in Hartford that is $44.48 an hour plus $29.74 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6.35% in Hartford. That is Connecticut's state rate.
page.buyers_extra: - **Insurance offices, state buildings and hospitals:** stainless steel or phenolic where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, powder coated steel or laminate on dry office floors.

Recheck https://portal.ct.gov/das/office-of-state-building-inspector/building-and-fire-code-adoption-process before launch and add a 'New rules on [date]' bullet once a date is set.

No Hartford ordinance on restroom signs or all-gender rooms was found in two web searches, but the Hartford Municipal Code (Municode) could not be opened by automated tools: check it once in a browser. The same goes for any city wage rule on city contracts.
